text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.8% today as oil prices dropped following news of U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks at the UN. The company's stock is down 7.2% over two weeks, directly tracking the collapse in crude prices—U.S. oil has fallen from much higher levels to $107 a barrel. When oil prices fall, integrated oil producers like ConocoPhillips see their profits compressed, since their earnings depend heavily on the price they can sell crude for.

The broader driver is geopolitical: hopes for a diplomatic solution to the U.S.-Iran conflict have reduced expectations of supply disruptions in the Middle East. Oil traders are pricing in a less severe shortage scenario, which removes the premium that had been built into prices. The uncertainty itself is also pressuring the stock—analysts have publicly acknowledged they don't know where oil prices will settle as the diplomatic situation remains fluid, making it harder for investors to value energy stocks with confidence.
